steps.title: The third unit
steps.body: Any play with a kick belongs to ==special teams==: kickoffs, punts, field goals and extra points. Field position swings on them.

steps.title: Kicker
steps.body: Kicks off and boots ==field goals and extra points==. A holder catches the snap and sets the ball down so the kicker can hit it.
steps.note: The holder is often the punter.

steps.title: Punter
steps.body: On 4th down too far from a field goal, the punter ==kicks it away== as far as he can. Losing the ball 40 yards downfield beats losing it right here.

steps.title: Long snapper
steps.body: A specialist who fires the ball ==about 15 yards back== to the punter, fast and on target. You only hear his name when ==something goes wrong==.

steps.title: Returner
steps.body: Catches kickoffs and punts and tries to ==run them back==. Usually one of the fastest players on the roster.

steps.title: Fair catch
steps.body: A punt returner who ==waves an arm overhead== is calling a fair catch. Nobody can hit him, but he ==can't run with it== after the catch.

steps.prompt: Why didn't anyone tackle the returner?
options: He caught it in the end zone
The punt went out of bounds
steps.explain: He waved his arm overhead before the ball came down. That's a fair catch: he's protected, the play ends, and his team starts from that spot.

steps.prompt: It's 4th and 15 at midfield. Who usually comes on?
options: The kicker, for a field goal
steps.explain: Midfield is too far for a field goal, and 15 yards is a lot to gain on one play. Most teams punt.
